title: Spend Search Where It Pays: Value-Guided Structured Sampling and Optimization for Generative Recommendation

problem.claim: Fine-tuning generative recommendation models with reinforcement learning suffers from a probability-reward mismatch, including insufficient exploration and advantage compression under likelihood-dominated decoding.

gap.claim: Conventional likelihood-dominated decoding does not adequately explore low-probability, high-reward branches or provide strong comparative reinforcement-learning signals.

contributions.claim: V-STAR is a value-guided sampling and tree-structured advantage reinforcement framework for generative recommendation.
Value-Guided Efficient Decoding selectively deepens high-potential prefixes by identifying decisive nodes without exhaustive tree search.
Sibling-GRPO uses induced tree topology to compute sibling-relative advantages and concentrate learning signals on decisive branching decisions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on offline and online datasets.
The authors report that V-STAR outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy and candidate-set diversity under strict latency constraints.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative recommendation unifies retrieval and ranking through conditional generation.
Reinforcement-learning fine-tuning faces a probability-reward mismatch, while conventional decoding causes insufficient exploration and advantage compression.
The paper proposes V-STAR, combining value-guided decoding with tree-structured advantage reinforcement.
VED selectively expands promising prefixes, and Sibling-GRPO computes sibling-relative advantages at decisive branches.
Experiments on offline and online datasets are reported to show improved accuracy and candidate-set diversity under strict latency constraints.

source_observation.claim: Likelihood-dominated decoding can prune low-probability branches before their potential reward is observed.

interpretation.claim: Search allocation may benefit from value-aware selective exploration rather than probability ranking alone.

application.claim: In sequential generation or decision systems, selectively deepen branches with high estimated potential when exhaustive search is too costly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when value-guided selective search is preferable across tasks, models, or latency regimes beyond the reported setting.

source_observation.claim: Trajectories sharing high-probability prefixes can have highly correlated rewards and low within-group variance.

interpretation.claim: Comparisons among structurally related sibling decisions may produce more informative reinforcement-learning signals.

application.claim: Use local, topology-aware relative advantages when learning depends on distinguishing alternative branches from a common prefix.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify whether sibling-relative advantages remain effective when the tree structure or reward comparisons are unreliable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the value estimator, training procedure, or latency measurements.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or generalization beyond the reported experiments.
